'''James L. Skinner''' (born August 17, 1953)<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Skinner|first=James L.|date=2014-07-17|title=Autobiography of James L. Skinner|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry B|volume=118|issue=28|pages=7671–7672|doi=10.1021/jp504477e|pmid=25031098|issn=1520-6106}}</ref> is an American [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemist]]. He is the [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder|Joseph O.]] and Elizabeth S. [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder|Hirschfelder]] Professor Emeritus at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University Wisconsin-Madison]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.wisc.edu/users/skinner|title=skinner {{!}} UW-Madison Department of Chemistry|website=www.chem.wisc.edu|language=en-us|access-date=2019-11-12|archive-date=2018-09-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911081758/https://www.chem.wisc.edu/users/skinner|url-status=dead}}</ref> Until 2024 he was a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Robert A. Welch Foundation|Welch Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.welch1.org/about/advisory-board|title=Scientific Advisory Board|website=www.welch1.org|access-date=2019-11-12}}</ref> Until 2020, Skinner was the Crown Family Professor of [[Molecular engineering|Molecular Engineering]], professor of [[chemistry]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/faculty/jim-skinner|title=Jim Skinner {{!}} University of Chicago Department of Chemistry|website=chemistry.uchicago.edu|access-date=2019-11-12|archive-date=2019-11-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112201138/https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/faculty/jim-skinner|url-status=dead}}</ref> director of the Water Research Initiative and deputy dean for faculty affairs of [[Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering at the University of Chicago|the Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering]] at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pme.uchicago.edu/skinner_group/people/james_skinner/|title=James Skinner – People – Skinner Group – Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering|website=pme.uchicago.edu|access-date=2019-11-12|archive-date=2019-11-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112181752/https://pme.uchicago.edu/skinner_group/people/james_skinner/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Skinner is recognized for his contributions to the fields of [[theoretical chemistry]], nonequilibrium [[statistical mechanics]], linear and nonlinear [[spectroscopy]] of [[liquid]]s, [[Amorphous solid|amorphous]] and [[crystalline solids]], [[surface]]s, [[protein]]s, and [[supercritical fluid]]s. Skinner is the co-author of over 230 peer-reviewed research articles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=X-kCRA0AAAAJ&hl=en|title=James L. Skinner – Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2019-11-12}}</ref>

== Education ==
Skinner received his A. B. in chemistry and physics, both with highest honors, from the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] in 1975.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=James L. Skinner|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/james-l-skinner-7961qq/|access-date=2021-07-13|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> He received a Ph.D. in chemical physics from [[Harvard University]] in 1979 where he was a recipient of an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Graduate Fellowship and studied under the guidance of [[Peter Guy Wolynes|Peter G. Wolynes]]. The following year Skinner spent as an NSF Postdoctoral Fellow at [[Stanford University]], where he worked with Hans Andersen and [[Michael D. Fayer|Michael Fayer]].

== Career ==
Skinner joined the department of chemistry at [[Columbia University]] as an assistant professor of chemistry in 1981.<ref name=":2" /> He was promoted to associate professor in 1985 and became a professor of chemistry in 1986. In 1990, Skinner was appointed as the director of the Theoretical Chemistry Institute and became the [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder|Joseph O.]] and Elizabeth S. [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder|Hirschfelder]] Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]]. From 2004 to 2007, Skinner served as the chair of the department of chemistry at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.wisc.edu/content/department-history|title=Department History {{!}} UW-Madison Department of Chemistry|website=www.chem.wisc.edu|access-date=2019-11-12}}</ref> In 2015–2016, he served on the University of Wisconsin Campus Planning Committee and the Academic Planning Council. Skinner resigned his position as the director of the Theoretical Chemistry Institute and retired from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]] in December 2016, where he currently holds the title of [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder|Joseph O.]] and Elizabeth S. [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder|Hirschfelder]] Professor Emeritus. In January 2017, Skinner joined the Institute for Molecular Engineering (now [[Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering at the University of Chicago|Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering]]) at the [[University of Chicago]] as the Crown Family Professor of Molecular Engineering.<ref>{{Cite web|title=James Skinner|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/profile/james-skinner|access-date=2021-07-13|website=news.uchicago.edu|language=en|archive-date=2021-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713130538/https://news.uchicago.edu/profile/james-skinner|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also served as the director of the Water Research Initiative and deputy dean for faculty affairs at the [[Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering at the University of Chicago|Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering]]. In 2020, he moved back to his position at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin]].

== Professional service ==
During his career Skinner has held multiple professional appointments. From 1993 to 1996, he was, consequently, the vice-chair, chair-elect, and chair of the theoretical subdivision of the physical division of the [[American Chemical Society]] and from 2000 to 2004 he was the vice-chair-elect, vice-chair, vice-chair and then chair of the Gordon Conference on Molecular Electronic Spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.grc.org/electronic-spectroscopy-and-dynamics-conference/2003/|title=2003 Electronic Spectroscopy and Dynamics Conference GRC|website=www.grc.org|access-date=2019-11-12}}</ref> In 2007, he was a member of the Committee of Visitors of the [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Chemistry Division. From 2007 to 2010, Skinner was a member-at-large of the chemical physics division of the American Physical Society. From 2011 to 2014, he was the vice-chair, chair-elect, and the chair of chemical physics division of the [[American Physical Society]]. Since 2008 Skinner was a vice-chair and in 2014 he was the chair of American Conference on Theoretical Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telluridescience.org/for-scientists/for-participants/actc|title=ACTC {{!}} TSRC|website=www.telluridescience.org|access-date=2019-11-12}}</ref> While at the University of Chicago, Skinner actively participated in the [[University of Chicago]]-[[Argonne National Laboratory]] partnership by serving on the advisory board of the [[Argonne National Laboratory|Midwest Integrated Center for Computational Materials]] in 2016. Since 2015, he is an active member of the scientific advisory board of the [[Robert A. Welch Foundation|Welch Foundation]]. Since 2017, Skinner has been actively involved in the governance of the Telluride Science and Research Center (TSRC). From 2017 to 2019, he was a member of the board of directors of TSRC, becoming president of TSRC in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telluridescience.org/about/governance|title=Governance & Staff {{!}} TSRC|website=www.telluridescience.org|access-date=2019-11-12}}</ref>

=== Editorial service ===
Skinner has served on editorial boards of several scientific journals, including ''Single Molecules'' (2000–2003), ''[[Journal of Physical Chemistry]]'' (2004–2006), [[Chemical Physics (journal)|''Chemical Physics'']] (2005–2009), and [[Molecular Physics (journal)|''Molecular Physics'']] (2008–2014).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celebrating the career of Prof. James Skinner {{!}} Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering {{!}} The University of Chicago|url=https://pme.uchicago.edu/news/celebrating-career-prof-james-skinner|access-date=2021-07-13|website=pme.uchicago.edu|date=18 March 2020 |language=en}}</ref> Skinner had a long-standing relationship with ''[[The Journal of Chemical Physics]]''. In 1999, he joined the editorial board, and became an associate editor in 2009. Since 2015, Skinner served as a deputy editor of ''The Journal of Chemical Physics'', retiring from his editorial service in 2019.
